HEIC decoder source and rebuild information

The heic-to 1.6.7 dependency identifies its embedded library as libheif
1.23.7. Its development guide gives the libheif/libde265 build steps below.
These are the upstream release source tarballs used to make the sources easy
to retrieve with this application. The tarballs are unmodified byte-for-byte
copies of release assets. Their SHA-256 values are listed in SHA256SUMS.

Upstream release assets:
  https://github.com/strukturag/libheif/releases/tag/v1.23.7
  https://github.com/strukturag/libde265/releases/tag/v1.0.16

Build recipe, as documented by heic-to 1.6.7 (macOS example):

  brew install cmake make pkg-config x265 libde265 libjpeg libtool
  brew install emscripten
  cd libheif-1.23.7
  mkdir buildjs && cd buildjs
  LIBDE265_VERSION=1.0.16 USE_UNSAFE_EVAL=0 USE_WASM=0 \
    ../build-emscripten.sh ..

The bundled heic-to README also documents a change to build-emscripten.sh's
EXPORTED_FUNCTIONS symbol extraction, using llvm-nm, grep, sed, and paste.
The official libheif source archive includes the original build-emscripten.sh.
Consult the full build procedure in ../heic-to-1.6.7/README.md.
The resulting library source is wrapped into the heic-to CSP worker by the
heic-to-1.6.7 build script and distributed here as
heic-to-1.6.7/dist/csp/heic-to.js and its underlying source files.

Upstream library license texts are preserved separately as
libheif-1.23.7-COPYING.txt and libde265-1.0.16-COPYING.txt; the full original
source archives also contain their license and copyright files. Do not assume
these are the only third-party components in a locally rebuilt library: the
recipe enables libde265 and disables AOM and WebCodecs, but a changed recipe
may include other libraries. Review the chosen build configuration and all
licenses before redistribution.

The web application source and package lockfile are published alongside the
build output under the MIT License. Replace the decoder by changing the
dependency/build inputs and rebuilding the application. No technical measure
in this repository prevents relinking or reverse engineering the LGPL
components.
